title: DigitalOcean Launches Learning and Data Services to Enable Self-Improving AI Agents
gist: DigitalOcean put Learning Services (Insights, Signals, Simulations) and Agent Data Services into preview, building a closed loop where agent sessions feed evaluation and improvement on its own cloud. Commentators argue the outcome write-back loop, which turns agent logs into production data, matters more than retrieval.

insights.claim: DigitalOcean now positions its AI stack as a three-layer agent platform: Inference Engine for thinking, Managed Agents for acting, and Learning plus Data Services for improving, all on one open cloud using customer data.
insights.so_what: Shows a mid-tier cloud trying to move up from raw compute to sticky, full-lifecycle agent tooling to compete with hyperscalers.
insights.quote: We built Inference Engine so agents could think, Managed Agents so they could act, and now Agent Learning Services and Agent Data Services so they can improve
insights.speaker: DigitalOcean

insights.claim: DigitalOcean Learning Services has three parts: Insights records agent activity, Signals finds failures and performance gaps, and Simulations tests candidate fixes in simulated conversations before deployment.
insights.so_what: Agent evaluation and observability, once a separate startup category, is being bundled into cloud platforms.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone

insights.claim: DigitalOcean's improved Inference Router picks models per task to trade off cost against quality, and reruns the same evaluations whenever new model versions arrive.
insights.so_what: Model routing turns model providers into interchangeable suppliers and squeezes their pricing power at the platform layer.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone

insights.claim: In DigitalOcean's design, Signals writes agent sessions into Agent Data Services, and the Optimizer draws training and test data from it only when the customer expressly opts in.
insights.so_what: Opt-in data use is a selling point to enterprises worried about their data being used to train models.
insights.quote: Optimizer draws its training and test data from it only where the customer expressly opts in
insights.locator: Agent Learning Services are built on
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone

insights.claim: Once agent traces, tool calls and outcomes feed evaluation or learning, they are no longer just logs; they become production data that needs production-grade governance.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Saring
insights.so_what: Points to rising demand for governed storage and lineage tooling for agent telemetry.
insights.quote: Once traces, tool calls and outcomes feed evaluation or learning, they stop being “just logs” and become production data.
insights.locator: Commenting on the announcement on LinkedId

insights.claim: Most teams building agent data layers put their effort into retrieval and neglect logging outcomes, so months later nobody can tell which tool calls actually worked and which only looked fine at the time.
insights.speaker: Deepanshu Udhwani
insights.so_what: Outcome logging and attribution is an underserved gap in the agent tooling market.
insights.quote: Most teams build great retrieval and skip logging outcomes properly, so six months later nobody can tell which tool calls actually worked versus which ones just looked fine in the moment.
insights.locator: On a similar note, senior engineer

insights.claim: Most agent stacks fail where tool calls report success but users abandon the session; the real bottleneck is being able to read the session the user actually experienced.
insights.speaker: Keith Zhai
insights.so_what: Technical success metrics hide failures that users feel, so user-outcome observability is where the value lies.
insights.quote: Green tool calls next to abandoned users is still where most agent stacks break.

insights.claim: DigitalOcean Insights, Signals and Evaluations (including Simulations) are in public preview, while Inference Router optimization and Agent Data Services are only in private preview.
insights.so_what: The data layer, the stickiest part, is the least mature, so revenue impact is still some way off.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
